title: 7.17.2 Sub-build: One object hits another
description: Press 1: one dummy's hit(other) makes the other take a hit, never below 0, and after(45, ...) lets the other one hit back a moment later.

steps.title: Run it
steps.instructions: The top says `Left: 20    Right: 20` and `Press 1`. Pressing 1 does nothing yet.

steps.title: Two methods
steps.instructions: Inside the class, below `isAlive()`, write `takeHit(n) { this.hp = max(this.hp - n, 0); }`. Below it, `hit(other) { other.takeHit(this.power); }`. Nothing calls them yet, so Run looks the same.
hints: In `hit(other)`, `this` is the dummy that hits and `other` is the one handed in.
`max(this.hp - n, 0)` is the bigger of the two numbers, so hp stops at 0.

steps.title: Press 1 to hit
steps.instructions: In `draw()`, below `background(...)`: `if (kb.presses('1') && left.isAlive() && right.isAlive()) { left.hit(right); note = 'Left hits Right'; }`. Run and press 1 a few times: Right goes 16, 12, 8, 4, 0, and stops at 0 instead of going below it.
hints: Click the canvas first, so the keys go to the sketch.

steps.title: Hit back, a moment later
steps.instructions: Inside that same `if`, below `note = 'Left hits Right';`, add `after(45, () => { if (right.isAlive()) { right.hit(left); note = 'Right hits back'; } });`. Run and press 1: Right drops at once, and about a second later Left drops by 3.
hints: `after(45, ...)` runs the function 45 frames later. `draw()` keeps running in the meantime.
Right checks it is still alive before it hits back: a dummy at 0 hp does not hit.

requirements.title: hp never below 0
requirements.description: takeHit takes the hit off hp with a floor at 0, using max or a test. Help: 7.17.1 (Reading: A method that hits another object, and after())

requirements.title: One object hits another
requirements.description: A method is handed the other dummy and makes it take the hit through its own takeHit, and the sketch calls that method. Help: 7.17.1 (Reading: A method that hits another object, and after())

requirements.title: The hit back comes after a pause
requirements.description: after is given a number of frames and a function to run later. Help: 7.17.1 (Reading: A method that hits another object, and after())

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch for "Sub-build: One object hits another". The task: give the Dummy class takeHit(n), which lowers hp by n but never below 0, and hit(other), which makes the other dummy take a hit of this one's power through its takeHit; when 1 is pressed and both are alive, left hits right, and after(45, ...) makes right hit back a moment later if it is still alive. Accept any names, helpers, ternaries, nested ifs, switch statements and semicolons; a line only in a comment or string does not count. Short, plain notes for a 14-year-old; never write corrected code.
